articles.highlight: 十四届全国人大常委会第二十五次会议表决通过《中华人民共和国南极活动与环境保护法》，明年1月1日起施行。

articles.title: The Relationship Between Comedy, Democracy, and AI
articles.highlight: 幽默是一种基本的人类自由：笑能保护我们免受一切使人非人化的东西——暴政、交易主义、囚禁与商品化。
articles.summary: 文章从弗兰克尔在霍尔ocaust中把幽默视为保持理智与生存的救生索出发，提出幽默是一种基本的人类自由，能让人暂时超脱处境。它进一步把共同的笑与自由社会、思想自由和民主联系起来，并把幽默理解为制造惊喜的艺术。适合想从人文角度理解幽默、民主与AI关系的人阅读。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键启示：幽默是保护人性与自由的基本能力，不应被简化为娱乐或交易；讨论AI与民主时，应重视这种维系共同人性的经验。
articles.sourceExcerpt: “Humor, more than anything else in the human make-up, can afford an aloofness and an ability to rise above any situation, even if only for a few seconds,” Viktor Frankl wrote in recalling the role of humor as a lifeline to sanity and survival in the Holocaust. Humor is a fundamental human freedom: To laugh is to protect ourselves from all that dehumanizes us — tyranny and transactionalism, captivity and commodification. Humor is also fundamental to free societies, to freedom of thought, to democracy: To laugh together is to harmonize our deepest humanity.

en.highlight: Humor is a fundamental human freedom: To laugh is to protect ourselves from all that dehumanizes us — tyranny and transactionalism, captivity and commodification.
en.summary: Starting from Viktor Frankl’s account of humor as a lifeline to sanity and survival in the Holocaust, the article presents humor as a basic human freedom that lets us rise above any situation, if only briefly. It links laughing together to free societies, freedom of thought, and democracy, and describes humor as the art of surprise. It is worth reading for a humanistic perspective on why humor matters beyond entertainment.
en.failureAnalysis: The key takeaway is that humor is a basic freedom that protects human dignity against tyranny and commodification; debates about AI and democracy should not reduce it to entertainment or a transaction.
en.title: The Relationship Between Comedy, Democracy, and AI

articles.sourceExcerpt: ROBUSTEEG-BASEDEMOTIONRECOGNITION FROMCOARSE TRIAL-LEVELLABELS UNDERINTRA-TRIALAFFECTIVE VARIABILITY A PREPRINT Xiaocong Zeng School of Mathematics (Zhuhai) Sun Yat-sen University Guangdong, 519082, CHINA zengxc3@mail2.sysu.edu.cn Buxuan Wang School of Computer Science and Engineering Sun Yat-sen University Guangdong, 510275, CHINA wangbx29@mail2.sysu.edu.cn Xin Yang School of Mathematics (Zhuhai) Sun Yat-sen University Guangdong, 519082, CHINA yangx367@mail2.sysu.edu.cn Pei Huang School of Mathematics (Zhuhai) Sun Yat-sen University Guangdong, 519082, CHINA huangpei1993@qq.com Dongyang Kuang School of Mathematics (Zhuhai) Sun Yat-sen University Guangdong, 519082, CHINA kuangdy@mail.sysu.edu.cn ABSTRACT EEG-based emotion recognition has become an active research area in brain–computer interfaces.
